evidence.locator: Supplementary Table2 row39, Individual35 GEL-recode3 D:F

limitations: Transcript version and genome reference sequence were not independently rederived.

segregation.statement: Heterozygous, de novo. Author-reported de novo status. Maternal allele, when stated, is origin of new allele, not inherited transmission.

evidence.locator: Supplementary Table2 row39, Individual35 GEL-recode3 F,BR

Gait disturbance: The source does not establish this exact negative assertion. No direct individual assertion of this precise phenotype identified in the complete source row. Narrative omission is not an explicit negative. Source: AQ15=[blank/not provided] | X15=2 years | AC15=(23mo) Developmentally, gross motor skills are progressing, now at the 8 month level. She sits steadily and transitions out of sitting using a side-sit positioning. She crawls reciprocally on hands and knees and can get herself back into a seated position. She can get herself into a high kneel position, but does not yet pull to stand. 
 
 Fine motor/play skills are also progressing, now in the 8-10 month range. Seated on her mother’s lap at the table surface, she displayed fair interest in people and objects in her environment. She reached for toys presented with either hand, although she continues to show right hand dominance (stronger and more refined). She obtained a block in either hand and transferred between hands. She retained a block in both hands and banged them at midline, and then obtained a third block when it was presented. She used her thumb in opposition to her fingers to pick up 1-cm beads although her mother reports a pincer grasp at home. She used her two hands together to lift an inverted cup rather than more precisely lifting it by its handle. She pulled a string to access a ring attached on the other end; she enjoyed chewing on the string but then suspended the ring in imitation. She obtained a bell and thoroughly enjoyed discovering it. She visually and manually explored its parts and then rang it with purpose. Object permanence is present in that she looked for an object that had fallen from the table surface, but she did not demonstrate a higher order search for the missing contents of a box. In terms of container play, she removed an item from a cup but she did not replace it (and is not yet doing so at home yet). She enjoyed pushing a car back and forth with the examiner. (28mo)- walks with a walker, finger feeding, not able to use utensils. causal_confidence.statement:
Strong recurrent-region gene association and de novo evidence; each patient still needs clinical interpretation. Additional source context: DARS2 carrier c.564+1G>A(mat)
 PPP1R15B c.980A>G (mat)
 Negative genome through UDP
 Negative microarray
 
 WGS, WES, Microarray, Mito genome have been previously nondiagnostic. WGS at NIH showed hemizygous VUS in ZNF674 gene c.-143G>T reported to cause neurodevelopmental disorders. Negative Methylation and copy number analysis for PWS and Fragile X. Normal Karyotype. Family trio genome was negative but had two variants of unknown clinical significance in PPP1R15B, inherited from mother known to cause microcephaly, and DARS, inherited from his mother known to cause hypomyelination of the brainstem and spinal cord and leg spasticity.

assessment.statement:
Delayed ability to walk: Source supports the recorded direction with qualification. Source reports later/assisted walking or not yet walking; age/context retained, no independent developmental assessment. Source: X13=Walking by age 5, ataxic gait | Y13=Y, abnormal gait | AC13=First concerns about development were noted at 4 months old (due to poor head control).
 Gross Motor: Walking has greatly improved, but still fatigues sooner than other children. Falls often. 
 Fine Motor: pincer grasp, writes with whole fist, mostly doing hand-over-hand for fine motor. 
 Speech / Cognition: Babbles. Has communication device that he uses more at school than at home. Does not point but will occasionally drag parents to what he wants. Usually brings things to parents to indicate wants. 
 Social / Others: Social laugh and interacts with parents
 Regression: regression in toileting
 Behavioral Problems: moves a lot. Hitting and scratching others more than before. Continues to communicate issues. Continues to have feeding issues. 
 
 Developmental concerns were initially raised at the four-month well-child check where patient was noted to have poor neck control, global hypotonia and poor eye contact. Gross motor skills included sitting independently and moving from sitting to his hands and knees. No independent standing or walking was observed. Did not yet display a refined pincer nor a sustained radial palmar grasp. Plays near other children and will, at times, show interest and watch other children play. Vineland 3 at 2 years of age is gross motor is 8 months, fine motor is 7 months, receptive is 5 months. Adaptive behavior composite score is 50. Significant cognitive and global developmental delays. Mullen Scale of Early Learning at age 2: Visual Reception is 11 months, Gross Motor 8 months, Fine Motor 4 months, Receptive Language 6 months, Expressive 5 months

49 detailed patients, 115 variant carriers overall. All49 source rows read. No patient raw genomic files inspected; this is post-inference source support, not clinical truth.

Critical18bpregion enrichment is strong association; 60/8841 undiagnosedGEL0.68% observed versus 0.4%allNDD estimate assumes40%prior diagnostic yield. No unselected prospective prevalence established. Main Results and ExtendedDataTable1.

Common n.64_65insT has one real UKBiobank heterozygote23reference/18alternate reads, age70–75 and nervous-system history ICDZ86.6. Do not claim universal control absence. SupplementaryTable1 PDFpp6–7.

Five bloodRNAseq cases vs378controls and10matchedcontrols. Novel5prime events unadjusted P3.95e-5 vs378, P0.00571 vs10 (ExtendedDataTable2); latter does not pass stated0.005 threshold. TotaloutliersP0.0126 vs378 not corrected significant. No neural/drugrescue measured.

54 phased de novo alleles maternal; maternal origin does not mean inherited. Elsewhere a mosaicmother and an inherited n.76C>T carrier reported. Do not apply those to specific S2 patients without matching identity.

Individual13 has GJB2 homozygous diagnosis explicitly accounting for hearing loss. Additional carrier/VUS findings in individuals3,9,14,19,24,28,29,33,34,36,47 and provisional mitochondrial labels17/45 are not proved alternative/multilocus diagnoses.

Packet positives show substantial patient-row mismapping, especially dysmorphology/MRI. Packet negatives frequently assert absence from unreported narrative; preserved as unresolved. S2 A1 explicitly says blank data not provided.

Source itself has internal conflicts: regression AG=N with developmental regression narratives in individuals9,23,24,45; clinical speech values and narrative differ (e.g24). Suspected findings remain qualified.
